items.title: Roll your shoulders back five times. Slowly.
items.sub: Slower than that. You rushed it just reading this.

items.title: Look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds.
items.sub: Twenty feet, twenty seconds. Your eyes have been at arm's length all morning.

items.title: Unclench your jaw. It was clenched.
items.sub: It was. It has been since the last prompt.

items.title: Drop your shoulders away from your ears.
items.sub: They crept up again somewhere around the third retry.

items.title: Stretch your wrists in both directions.
items.sub: Both directions, ten seconds each. They have typed a lot today.

items.title: Stand up. That is the whole task.
items.sub: No stretch, no walk. Just be a standing person for a moment.

items.title: Take one sip of water. Then another.
items.sub: You have had coffee and nothing else since breakfast.

items.title: Blink deliberately ten times to rehydrate your eyes.
items.sub: Staring at a screen halves your blink rate. This is the fix.

items.title: Tilt your head to each side for a five count.
items.sub: Ear toward shoulder, no forcing. Five slow counts a side.

items.title: Press your palms together and stretch your forearms.
items.sub: Prayer position, elbows out, press down. Ten seconds.

items.title: Point and flex your feet under the desk.
items.sub: Nobody can see. Twenty each way gets the blood moving.

items.title: Straighten your spine one vertebra at a time.
items.sub: Start at the tailbone and stack upward. It takes about ten seconds.

items.title: Squeeze your shoulder blades together and hold.
items.sub: Like you are holding a pencil between them. Hold for five.

items.title: Open and close your fists ten times.
items.sub: Wakes the hands up better than shaking them out does.

items.title: Breathe in for four, hold for four, out for four.
items.sub: Three rounds. The count matters more than the depth.

items.title: Name three sounds you can hear right now.
items.sub: One far away, one close, one you are making yourself.

items.title: Close your eyes until the model finishes.
items.sub: Nothing to watch. The spinner is not a progress bar.

items.title: Take one breath that is longer on the way out.
items.sub: In for four, out for six. That ratio is the whole trick.

items.title: Notice where your attention went. Bring it back.
items.sub: No judgement about where it went. Just notice, then return.

items.title: Put your phone face down.
items.sub: It will still be there. That is rather the point.

items.title: Look out a window. Any window.
items.sub: Distance is the thing your eyes are missing, not scenery.

items.title: Let your eyes go soft and unfocused for ten seconds.
items.sub: Let the screen blur. Focusing muscles get tired too.

items.title: Sigh out loud. It resets more than you think.
items.sub: Out loud. A real one. Your nervous system reads it as safety.

items.title: Read the last thing it wrote. The whole thing.
items.sub: Not the summary of it. The thing.

items.title: Stage the hunks you have actually read.
items.sub: The rest can wait for eyes.

items.title: Delete a log line neither of you meant to keep.
items.sub: It was debugging. It is not any more.

items.title: Write the commit message yourself.
items.sub: You know why. It only knows what.

items.title: Check the function it called actually exists.
items.sub: Confident is not the same as correct.

items.title: Read your last prompt back to yourself.
items.sub: Half of bad output is a fair reading of a bad ask.

items.title: Check which branch you are on.
items.sub: Both of you have been moving fast.

items.title: Save the file. Yes, that one.
items.sub: The one the last five minutes were about.

items.title: Count the files in the diff.
items.sub: A one-line fix that touched nine is a conversation.

items.title: Move one thing off your desk.
items.sub: One thing. Whichever one you keep moving out of the way.

items.title: Throw away the nearest piece of rubbish.
items.sub: It is within arm's reach and you have stopped seeing it.

items.title: Wipe a fingerprint off your screen.
items.sub: You have been reading through it for a week.

items.title: Untangle one cable.
items.sub: The one behind the monitor that is knotted around two others.

items.title: Put the pen back where the pen lives.
items.sub: Wherever that is. You know where that is.

items.title: Guess how long this run will take. Check later.
items.sub: Write the number down. Being wrong is the fun part.

items.title: Pick a colour and find five of it in the room.
items.sub: You will find seven. Rooms are more colourful than they look.

items.title: Spin once in your chair. You earned it.
items.sub: A full rotation. Chairs that spin should be spun.

items.title: Invent a worse name for the function you just wrote.
items.sub: The worse it is, the better you will remember what the function does.

items.title: Ask yourself what you are actually trying to ship.
items.sub: Not the ticket. The actual thing it is meant to make possible.

items.title: Notice one thing that went right today.
items.sub: Small counts. The bar is genuinely on the floor here.

items.title: Decide what the next single step is.
items.sub: One step. Not the plan, not the epic. The next step.

items.title: Say out loud what problem you are solving.
items.sub: Saying it out loud finds the hole in it faster than thinking does.

items.title: React to a teammate message with something kind.
items.sub: Costs nothing, lands better than you expect.

items.title: Say good morning to whoever is nearby.
items.sub: If nobody is nearby, this one is a free skip.

items.title: Read one line of the changelog for your framework.
items.sub: One line. You have been on this version for eight months.

items.title: Hover a symbol and read its actual type.
items.sub: The inferred one, not the one you assume it is.

items.title: Look up one flag on the command you just ran.
items.sub: The flag you copied from a blog post in 2022.

items.title: Do a lap of the room. Two if it is small.
items.sub: Perimeter only. The point is the moving, not the distance.

items.title: Ten slow squats next to your chair.
items.sub: Slow down means slow. Two seconds down, two seconds up.

items.title: Hang forward and let your head dangle.
items.sub: Knees soft, arms heavy. Come up one vertebra at a time.

items.title: Refill your water bottle properly.
items.sub: Not a top-up. Walk to the tap and fill the whole thing.

items.title: Do a doorway chest stretch on both sides.
items.sub: Forearm on the frame, step through, turn away. Thirty seconds a side.

items.title: Stand on one leg until you wobble. Switch.
items.sub: Then close your eyes and try again. Much harder.

items.title: Raise your desk and stand for this whole run.
items.sub: If it goes up, put it up. One run standing is a fair trade.

items.title: Twenty jumping jacks. Nobody is watching.
items.sub: And if they are, they are also waiting on a model.

items.title: Stretch your hip flexors. You sit too much.
items.sub: Half kneeling, tuck the pelvis, lean forward. It will complain.

items.title: Walk to the furthest window and back.
items.sub: Furthest one, not the nearest one. Make it an actual trip.

items.title: Hold a plank for as long as the spinner spins.
items.sub: Rough and honest. Down when the shaking starts.

items.title: Massage the base of your skull with both thumbs.
items.sub: Where the skull meets the neck. Small circles, real pressure.

items.title: Box breathing: four in, four hold, four out, four hold. Five rounds.
items.sub: Five rounds is about ninety seconds. Count them properly.

items.title: Sit still and do absolutely nothing. On purpose.
items.sub: Not scrolling. Not planning. The doing-nothing is the exercise.

items.title: Put on one song and just listen to it.
items.sub: The whole song, start to finish, without a second tab.

items.title: Step outside and feel the actual weather.
items.sub: Whatever it is doing out there, go and be in it briefly.

items.title: Make a cup of tea without checking anything.
items.sub: The kettle is a legitimate use of a two minute wait.

items.title: Body scan from your scalp down to your feet.
items.sub: Scalp, jaw, shoulders, hands, hips, feet. Notice, do not fix.

items.title: Turn off every notification for the next hour.
items.sub: One hour. You can turn them back on afterwards.

items.title: Splash cold water on your face.
items.sub: Works on tiredness far better than the fourth coffee will.

items.title: Stare at a plant. Plants are good for this.
items.sub: No task attached. Just look at the plant.

items.title: Check the test it wrote actually asserts something.
items.sub: A green test that cannot fail is just a green light.

items.title: Read the diff before you commit it. Properly.
items.sub: Line by line, like it came from a stranger. It did.

items.title: Rename one thing it named after the pattern.
items.sub: `DataServiceHandler` tells you nothing and it knows.

items.title: Delete the try/catch that swallows the error.
items.sub: It added that so the tests would pass.

items.title: Break the thing on purpose and watch the test fail.
items.sub: If it still passes, it was never watching.

items.title: Check whether that TODO is still true.
items.sub: Some of them were fixed three prompts ago.

items.title: Prune your merged local branches.
items.sub: One per idea you had this week. There were many.

items.title: Write down the bug you noticed but did not file.
items.sub: You will not remember it after the next prompt.

items.title: Look up the API it used, in the real documentation.
items.sub: Plausible method names are the whole problem.

items.title: Say what you are building, out loud, in one sentence.
items.sub: If you cannot, the next prompt will not go well either.

items.title: Improve one error message so it names the fix.
items.sub: Future you will be reading it at speed.

items.title: Check the dependency it added is one you want to own.
items.sub: It picked the first one that fit. You keep it forever.

items.title: Add the comment explaining the bit that surprised you.
items.sub: Surprise is the part nobody can regenerate.

items.title: Run it. Actually run it.
items.sub: Reading is not running, however good it looks.

items.title: Check it changed nothing else while it was in there.
items.sub: Helpful is a strong word for some of those edits.

items.title: Read the docs page for the thing you are currently guessing at.
items.sub: The page you have been substituting with confident guessing.

items.title: Look up one keyboard shortcut and use it three times.
items.sub: Three uses is roughly where it starts to stick.

items.title: Read the release notes of a tool you use daily.
items.sub: You upgraded it without reading them. Everyone does.

items.title: Skim one file in the codebase you have never opened.
items.sub: Every codebase has one. Pick it and read the top half.

items.title: Find out what that acronym in the ticket actually means.
items.sub: Everyone in the thread is also quietly unsure.

items.title: Read one man page top to bottom.
items.sub: Actually to the bottom. There are options down there you will want.

items.title: Learn what one environment variable in your config does.
items.sub: You inherited it and have never touched it out of respect.

items.title: Read the first paragraph of a spec you cite often.
items.sub: Just the first paragraph. Specs are less hostile than they look.

items.title: Clear your downloads folder of last week.
items.sub: Everything from before Monday can go without ceremony.

items.title: Close every terminal tab you are not using.
items.sub: You have nine open and you are using two of them.

items.title: Archive the chat threads that are finished.
items.sub: The decision was made. The thread does not need to stay open.

items.title: Empty the mug graveyard on your desk.
items.sub: There are at least two. Take them all in one trip.

items.title: Rename the four screenshots on your desktop.
items.sub: Screenshot 2026-08-14 at 11.42.07 tells you nothing.

items.title: Sort today inbox into reply, archive, ignore.
items.sub: Three piles, no fourth. The fourth pile is how inboxes die.

items.title: Delete the branch you merged three weeks ago.
items.sub: It merged cleanly and has been loitering ever since.

items.title: Send a teammate the answer you found yesterday.
items.sub: You solved it and then said nothing. Send them the answer.

items.title: Approve the pull request that has been sitting there.
items.sub: It is small, you already skimmed it, and they are blocked.

items.title: Thank whoever unblocked you last week.
items.sub: They will have forgotten. It will still land well.

items.title: Reply to the message you keep marking unread.
items.sub: One sentence is a complete reply. They are not expecting an essay.

items.title: Leave one genuinely useful code review comment.
items.sub: One that helps. Not a nit about a space before a brace.

items.title: Ask someone what they are stuck on.
items.sub: Best question on any team. Costs you thirty seconds.

items.title: Try to beat your own typing speed record.
items.sub: Loser buys nobody anything. Purely for the numbers.

items.title: Give your branch a ridiculous but accurate name.
items.sub: Accurate first, ridiculous second. Both are achievable.

items.title: Doodle the architecture as if it were a city.
items.sub: Services become districts, queues become roads. It clarifies more than it should.

items.title: Read the funniest commit message in your repo history.
items.sub: Search the log for a swear word. Start there.

items.title: Write a haiku about the bug you are fixing.
items.sub: Five, seven, five. The bug deserves the formality.

items.title: Write one sentence about what you learned this morning.
items.sub: One sentence. If nothing comes, that is also information.

items.title: Ask whether this task is still worth finishing.
items.sub: Sunk cost is not a reason. It is allowed to be no.

items.title: Check your calendar for the thing you forgot.
items.sub: There is something in there you have not looked at properly.

items.title: Write tomorrow first task on a sticky note.
items.sub: Tomorrow morning you will be extremely grateful for that note.

items.title: Name the assumption you have not tested yet.
items.sub: There is one. Write it down before the answer arrives.

items.title: Go for a proper walk around the block.
items.sub: Coat on, door shut, actual pavement. Ten minutes is plenty.

items.title: Do a short mobility routine for your spine and hips.
items.sub: Cat-cow, hip circles, thoracic rotations. Whatever you remember.

items.title: Make real food instead of the snack you were going to have.
items.sub: You were going to eat crisps standing up over the sink.

items.title: Stretch everything that hurts, gently, one at a time.
items.sub: One at a time, and stop before it becomes interesting.

items.title: Climb the stairs in your building to the top.
items.sub: All the way up. The lift is not part of this task.

items.title: Fix your chair height, monitor height, and keyboard angle.
items.sub: Ten minutes now against the neck you will have at forty.

items.title: Lie on the floor with your legs up a wall.
items.sub: Legs vertical, five minutes. Absurdly effective on tired legs.

items.title: Do a ten minute guided meditation.
items.sub: Pick any one. The picking is not the important part.

items.title: Sit somewhere different in your home and look around.
items.sub: A different chair genuinely changes what you notice.

items.title: Take a shower. Genuinely the best debugger available.
items.sub: Nobody knows why it works. It reliably works.

items.title: Eat lunch away from every screen you own.
items.sub: Every screen. The phone counts as a screen.

items.title: Nap for ten minutes with an alarm set.
items.sub: Set the alarm first. Ten minutes, not forty.

items.title: Read a file you have not opened since it rewrote it.
items.sub: You own this now, whoever typed it.

items.title: Write the design note before the next prompt.
items.sub: Thinking first is cheaper than three rounds of fixing.

items.title: Write the test for the part you could not debug alone.
items.sub: That is the part that will break at the worst moment.

items.title: Tidy the git history before you open the PR.
items.sub: Nine commits called "fix" is a story nobody can read.

items.title: Trace one request end to end, asking nothing.
items.sub: Just you and the code. It goes better than you expect.

items.title: Profile the slow endpoint you have been ignoring.
items.sub: Nobody has ever guessed this correctly, including it.

items.title: Delete the abstraction that has exactly one caller.
items.sub: It was being helpful about a future that never came.

items.title: Explain the change out loud as if you wrote it.
items.sub: The gaps in the explanation are the gaps in the code.

items.title: Split the giant function into the three things it does.
items.sub: It grew a limb every time you asked for one more thing.

items.title: Read a whole blog post instead of skimming three.
items.sub: All the way through, one tab, no skimming.

items.title: Work through one exercise in a language you are learning.
items.sub: One exercise beats another hour of tutorial video.

items.title: Read the source of a library you depend on.
items.sub: You import it daily and have never opened it. Go and look.

items.title: Watch a conference talk at 1.5x and take one note.
items.sub: One note. If you cannot find one, the talk was not for you.

items.title: Read the RFC behind the protocol you use every day.
items.sub: It is drier than the blog posts and about four times more correct.

items.title: Reimplement a small utility from scratch to see how it works.
items.sub: Sixty lines will teach you more than the docs did.

items.title: Triage your issue tracker down to what is actually real.
items.sub: Close anything nobody has mentioned in three months.

items.title: Reorganise your project folder the way you always meant to.
items.sub: You have known the right structure since about week two.

items.title: Clean your keyboard properly. It is worse than you think.
items.sub: Turn it over first. Try not to look directly at what falls out.

items.title: Update your dotfiles and commit them.
items.sub: The change you made in a hurry is still uncommitted.

items.title: Back up the thing you would cry about losing.
items.sub: You know exactly which thing that is.

items.title: Review a colleague pull request properly, not just approve it.
items.sub: Read it to understand it, not to make the badge go away.

items.title: Write the status update nobody asked for but everyone wants.
items.sub: Three bullets: shipped, stuck, next. That is the whole format.

items.title: Pair with someone for the length of one model run.
items.sub: One run's worth. Long enough to be useful, short enough to commit to.

items.title: Answer a question in a community forum.
items.sub: You know something that somebody is currently stuck on.

items.title: Call someone who is not a coworker.
items.sub: No agenda, no purpose. That is what makes it work.

items.title: Play one round of a game you can quit instantly.
items.sub: Quit instantly is the key requirement here.

items.title: Learn one card trick badly.
items.sub: Badly is the correct standard for a first attempt.

items.title: Build something small and pointless in CSS.
items.sub: No purpose, no ticket, no users. Just a nice gradient.

items.title: Solve one puzzle from an advent-of-code style set.
items.sub: One of the early ones. The late ones are not a break.

items.title: Journal about what actually slowed you down this week.
items.sub: Not what you did. What got in the way of what you did.

items.title: Review your last five commits and grade them honestly.
items.sub: Would you approve them from someone else? Be honest.

items.title: Write the plan for the rest of the day in three bullets.
items.sub: Three. Not eight. Three is a plan, eight is a wish.

items.title: Ask what you would tell a junior engineer to do here.
items.sub: You always give better advice when it is not your problem.

items.title: Go outside for a real walk. Leave the laptop.
items.sub: Phone in the pocket, laptop on the desk. It stays there.

items.title: Do a full workout. The run will still be running.
items.sub: It will. That is the strange luxury of a long generation.

items.title: Cook something that takes attention.
items.sub: Something with chopping in it. Chopping is the point.

items.title: Go to the gym. This is a long one.
items.sub: Genuinely long enough. Go.

items.title: Take a real break. Set a timer and step fully away.
items.sub: Timer first, then leave. Without the timer you will hover.

items.title: Read a chapter of a physical book.
items.sub: Paper. A chapter is about the right size for a long one.

items.title: Go and sit somewhere with no screens at all.
items.sub: No screens at all. Take a drink and sit there.

items.title: Do the errand you have been postponing for two weeks.
items.sub: Fourteen days of thinking about it, twenty minutes to do it.

items.title: Read a module you own end to end.
items.sub: Own is doing some work in that sentence.

items.title: Write the architecture doc properly, with diagrams.
items.sub: The one thing that does not regenerate from a prompt.

items.title: Pay down the debt item at the top of the list.
items.sub: It has been at the top for a reason.

items.title: Set up the check that would have caught last week's bug.
items.sub: Reviewing faster is not the same as catching it.

items.title: Migrate one module off the deprecated API.
items.sub: Before the training data catches up and insists on it.

items.title: Work through a full tutorial start to finish.
items.sub: Start to finish, including the boring setup section.

items.title: Read a paper you have had open in a tab for a month.
items.sub: It has survived four browser restarts. Read it or close it.

items.title: Build a toy version of the system you are trying to understand.
items.sub: Building a bad version teaches you what the good one is for.

items.title: Take the course module you bought and never opened.
items.sub: One module. You already paid for the whole thing.

items.title: Do a proper inbox zero pass.
items.sub: Every message gets a decision. No message gets read twice.

items.title: Clean your whole desk setup, cables included.
items.sub: Under the desk too. That is where the real situation is.

items.title: Audit and delete the cloud resources nobody is using.
items.sub: Somebody is paying for those. It is you.

items.title: Write the long reply to the person who deserves one.
items.sub: They wrote you something thoughtful. Match it.

items.title: Mentor someone for half an hour.
items.sub: Half an hour, a real question, no slides.

items.title: Write up what you learned so the next person does not have to.
items.sub: You worked it out the hard way. Write down the short way.

items.title: Build the silly demo you described to someone last month.
items.sub: You described it with your hands. That is usually a good sign.

items.title: Learn the first sixteen bars of something on an instrument.
items.sub: Sixteen bars is a real, finishable amount of music.

items.title: Do a personal retro on the last two weeks of work.
items.sub: Two weeks is long enough to see a pattern and short enough to remember.

items.title: Rewrite your task list from scratch instead of editing it.
items.sub: The ones that survive being retyped are the ones that matter.

items.title: Decide what you are going to stop doing.
items.sub: Stopping something is a decision. Make it deliberately.

chains.title: Reset the desk
chains.sub: Four small things. Stop wherever the answer lands.
steps: Clear everything off the desk that does not live there.
Wipe the surface. Yes, properly, with the thing you never use.
Untangle the cable that has been annoying you for a month.
Put one object back deliberately, where you actually want it.

chains.title: Unstick your shoulders
chains.sub: Four minutes of undoing a morning at a keyboard.
steps: Roll your shoulders backwards ten times, slower than feels useful.
Clasp your hands behind your back and open your chest. Thirty seconds.
Drop one ear towards one shoulder and breathe. Then the other side.
Stand up and reach for the ceiling as if you meant it.

chains.title: Come back down
chains.sub: For when the last hour has been a lot.
steps: Box breathing: four in, four hold, four out, four hold. Five rounds.
Name five things you can see without moving your head.
Drink a full glass of water. All of it.
Look at something more than twenty feet away for a minute.

chains.title: Read what you shipped
chains.sub: Three passes over work you did not type.
steps: Read the whole diff, not the summary of it.
Check one test actually fails when you break the thing.
Delete the comment that only restates the line under it.

chains.title: Empty the inbox a bit
chains.sub: Three passes. Not to zero, just to less.
steps: Archive everything you will obviously never read.
Reply to the one that takes under a minute.
Move the one you are avoiding to tomorrow, on purpose, with a time.

chains.title: Actually move
chains.sub: Three bursts. Your legs have been folded for hours.
steps: Ten slow squats next to the chair.
Walk to the furthest window in the building and look out of it.
Shake out your hands and wrists for thirty seconds.

chains.title: Work out what you are doing
chains.sub: Three questions, out loud if nobody is listening.
steps: Say what problem you are solving. Out loud.
Say what you would try if this approach is wrong.
Write the one sentence you would put in the pull request.

chains.title: Be a person for five minutes
chains.sub: Three things that are not work.
steps: Message someone you have been meaning to message.
Say something specific and nice to a colleague about their work.
Make a plan with an actual date in it.
